job.style: a description of a classroom activity or experiment and what it shows

passage: In our history class today, we explored how ancient trade and travel shaped India. We learned that the Silk Route was not just one single road, but a vast network of paths connecting China to the West. Traders used these routes to exchange goods, while sailors relied on the predictable monsoon winds to travel across the sea, rather than fearing them as storms. We also discussed the famous Chinese pilgrims like Fa Xian and Xuan Zang. They did not come to India to conquer land for their emperors; instead, they traveled thousands of miles to visit sacred sites and collect Buddhist manuscripts. Furthermore, we looked at the southern kingdoms, such as the Pallavas and Chalukyas. History shows they were not always peaceful allies; they frequently fought intense battles against each other to gain power. Finally, we examined the 'Sabha' in local village assemblies. We discovered that it was not a meeting where every villager could vote, but rather an exclusive assembly of wealthy brahmin landowners. By studying these facts, we see how complex and active the ancient world really was, far different from the simple stories we sometimes imagine.

items.evidence: Traders used these routes to exchange goods, while sailors relied on the predictable monsoon winds to travel across the sea, rather than fearing them as storms.
items.q: Why did ancient sailors plan their sea journeys around the monsoon winds?
options: The winds came at a known time each year
The winds were storms that stopped all ships
The winds blew along the Silk Route roads
The winds were rare, so trips were few
items.explain: Sailors relied on monsoon winds because they were predictable, not storms to fear.

wrong.why: thinks monsoon winds were dangerous storms
mixes up the sea route with land routes
misses that the winds were predictable

items.evidence: They did not come to India to conquer land for their emperors; instead, they traveled thousands of miles to visit sacred sites and collect Buddhist manuscripts.
items.q: What would Fa Xian most likely carry back to China after his journey?
options: Maps of lands won for his emperor
Silk goods bought from Indian traders
Gold given by Indian kings as gifts
items.explain: Fa Xian came to visit sacred sites and collect Buddhist manuscripts, not to conquer land.

wrong.why: thinks pilgrims came to conquer land
thinks the visits were royal gift trips

items.evidence: History shows they were not always peaceful allies; they frequently fought intense battles against each other to gain power.
items.q: Which best describes how the Pallavas and Chalukyas got along?
options: Rivals who often fought for more power
Friends at peace because both were southern
Allies who fought together against others
Neighbours who never met or traded
items.explain: The Pallavas and Chalukyas frequently fought battles against each other to gain power.

wrong.why: thinks southern kingdoms were always at peace
misreads 'allies' and misses who they fought

items.evidence: We discovered that it was not a meeting where every villager could vote, but rather an exclusive assembly of wealthy brahmin landowners.
items.q: Who took part in deciding matters in a village Sabha?
options: A few rich brahmins who owned land
Every villager, each casting one vote
Only the poorest farmers of the village
Officers sent by the Pallava king
items.explain: The Sabha was only for wealthy brahmin landowners; ordinary villagers could not vote.

wrong.why: thinks the Sabha was open to all villagers
reverses who held power in the village
picks a nearby kingdom name from the passage
